newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 9.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
MARKETING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - A conference on Internet commerce sponsored by the European Union agrees in principle there will be no new trade barriers or taxes imposed on companies or individuals wishing to do business in cyberspace. But the conference, attended by 40 government ministers from Europe, the United States, Japan and Canada, appeared to make little progress on how to regulate encryption technology needed for transaction security on the Internet. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The number of new books published in German dropped sharply in 1996 compared to the previous year but the industry still posted growth in sales, the Association of the German Book Industry says. With 71,500 new titles published last year, the association says production volume sank by 3.6 percent from 1995. (Reuter)

BONN - Four out of five Germans over 14 years old read a newspaper every day, which provides the medium with 50 million daily readers, the Association of German Newspaper Publishers (BDZV) says. (Reuter)
MUNICH - Nickelodeon, the children's station, boosted the size of its main target audience in Germany by 5.8 percent, media marketing company MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) says. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Bertelsmann New Media plans to offer new games and a 24-hour news service on the Internet and on AOL in the next few months. (Kress)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BERLIN - Germany is failing to make itself more competitive and is losing market share to leaner, meaner foreign competitors, a survey of leading German economic groups conducted by Die Welt newspaper shows. According to the survey, several of the associations put the blame for Germany's lack of competitiveness on high labour costs and taxes. The BGA Federation of German Wholesale and Export Trade says, for example, "We have enough work in Germany, but it is too expensive." (Reuter)

KITZBUEHEL, Austria - Compaq Computer Corp says it expects its business in Europe to expand faster than the market as a whole in 1997 as it broadens its product lines to reach new consumers and corporate customers. The company plans to launch 130 new products in Europe in the second half of the year -- including a series of home Pcs -- while streamlining its distribution and other operations, the company says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Chrysler Corp, citing strong demand for its minivans and Jeep vehicles, says it is strengthening its European dealer network in hopes of doubling sales within the next five to seven years. Chrysler Europe President Timothy Adams also tells Reuters that Chrysler has no plans to buy or set up new vehicle production sites in Europe. (Reuter)

BONN - Encouraged by the recent success of regulatory challenges against Deutsche Telekom AG, two of the phone giant's rivals file fresh complaints that, if successful, could lead to more competition. Telekom's two main domestic rivals, Mannesmann Arcor AG and O.Tel.O, file complaints with the Post and Telecommunications Ministry in Bonn, urging the government to intervene in negotiations over prices for network access.
(Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Ymos AG, an auto parts maker, says its financial performance has improved, but it still lost about five million marks ($2.8 million) in the first six months of 1997. (Reuter)

SCHWERIN - A European Union expert arrives on the northern German island of Ruegen to examine 170 tonnes of beef which officials suspect is British meat exported in defiance of a worldwide ban. (Reuter)
BONN - A recent rally in the price of cocoa futures could force Germany's chocolate industry to raise retail prices in the autumn of 1997, according to the confectionery association BDS.
(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Dirk Kruessenberg is new general manager for company customers at Otelo Communication GmbH, the telecommunications unit of Veba and RWE. Kruessenberg was previously vice president for Europe at Ralston Energy Systems. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Paulus Neef, senior partner of multimedia agency Pixelpark in Berlin, is now a member of the management board of Bertlesmann mediaSystems. Pixelpark is part of Bertelsmann. (Kress)
